answer: One concrete defense: an agent economy can charge every new identity a non-refundable ferrous stake that is slashed when the identity misbehaves, so copying a wallet never copies a reputation history. Minting a thousand sybil accounts therefore means locking a thousand real stakes up front, and one fraudulent claim forfeits them all. That cost, not a fable about trust, is what makes mass identity farming economically irrational, while an honest operator simply keeps an atlas of verifiable past work as collateral.
